changes.summary:
They keep the options of the 20261017 presets and add:

- Enums read as their const (`--use-single-value-enum-as-const`): Read an enum of one value, and an enum that admits the const beside it, as that const, so it renders as a Literal value instead of an enum class; one-value enum branches of a oneOf or anyOf merge into one enum.
- OpenAPI schemas modeled as definitions (`--openapi-as-definitions paths-bodies ref-components`): Give the request and response bodies of the OpenAPI paths and webhooks scopes the model a schema definition of the same body gets, so an object body with a type array such as [object, null] is a model instead of an inline type, and give an OpenAPI component written as a $ref to a recursive schema with sibling keywords the root model a definitions entry of the same schema gets, instead of no model.
- Site models for constrained references (`--use-site-models-for-constrained-refs`): Give an allOf of $ref members whose other parts add constraints, an enum or a type its own model of the values all parts admit, instead of the referenced type, which leaves the added assertions out; an allOf of enum references gets the enum of the members they share.
- Redundant constraints omitted (`--omit-redundant-constraints`): Do not write a constraint again beside a type that already enforces it: the bound of a zero-bound class such as NonNegativeInt, and the length and number constraints a const or enum Literal meets by its values, which also keeps such a const branch inline instead of a root model.
- Const read beside an enum (`--read-const-beside-enum`): Read a const beside an enum as JSON Schema does: a value is typed by the const that narrows the enum, and an enum that admits its const is read as that const.
- Literal values filtered (`--filter-literal-values`): Keep only the values of a const or enum that meet the length, pattern, bound and multipleOf constraints beside them.
- allOf keywords intersected (`--intersect-allof-keywords`): Combine the keywords of every part of an allOf, a $ref with sibling keywords and an inherited property override as JSON Schema validates them: the tightest bounds and the values every part admits.
- Nullable beside a type list (`--read-nullable-beside-type-list`): Write the null that nullable: true declares beside a type list with an object into the root model of that schema under strict nullable output.
- Field defaults kept off branch roots (`--keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots`): Leave the default of a property off the root models extracted from the branches of its anyOf or oneOf.
- Tuples for closed arrays (`--use-tuple-for-closed-arrays`): Generate tuple types for positional arrays that no other item can follow, so that each position keeps its own type.
- One dict for object maps (`--use-single-dict-for-object-maps`): Type an object map whose keys patternProperties or propertyNames constrain as one dict of the values of every key class.
- Stricter pattern-map checks (`--check-pattern-maps-strictly`): Under --generate-schema-validators, count every key that a pattern admits, check declared keys against the patterns that match them, and keep the propertyNames keys and the other types of a type array of an object without properties.
- Typed map values beside other types (`--use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types`): Under --use-typed-nullable-map-values, also type the map values of a type array that lists object beside other types, such as [object, string].
- Enum member values kept (`--keep-enum-member-values`): Write an enum as a plain Enum where its IntEnum, StrEnum or (T, Enum) base would change a member value, such as 2.5 beside integer members.
- Unevaluated properties read (`--read-unevaluated-properties`): Read a schema-valued unevaluatedProperties as additionalProperties where no applicator evaluates the object in place.
- Aliases pinned beside an alias generator (`--pin-aliases-with-alias-generator`): Write the generated alias on every field of a pydantic dataclass whose config names an alias generator, for pydantic versions older than 2.8.
- msgspec tags by payload name (`--tag-msgspec-by-payload-name`): Tag the structs of a discriminated union with the property name the document carries instead of the Python name it resolves to.
- Constructor fields ordered by final names and written defaults (`--order-constructor-fields-by final-names written-defaults`): Order the constructor fields of dataclass and msgspec models after every field has its final name, and the fields of msgspec and Pydantic dataclass models by the defaults they write.
- Request and response variants deduplicated (`--dedupe-request-response-variants`): Decide Request and Response variants from the schema graph and build each inline model once.
- Redundant reference null omitted (`--omit-redundant-reference-null`): Do not write None again where a field references a model that holds null itself.
- Decimal in field forms (`--use-decimal-in-field-forms`): Under --use-decimal-for-multiple-of, write Decimal for a number with multipleOf in the field forms too, and make it strict under --strict-types float.
- Shared parent wrappers collapsed (`--collapse-shared-parent-wrappers`): Under the parent name strategy, collapse a wrapper in every model that references it instead of keeping it for the models after the first.
changes.title: New dated presets `standard-py3XX-20261027` and `practical-py3XX-20261027`

changes.summary:
They keep the options of the 20261027 presets and add:

- Shared variant tags merged (`--merge-shared-variant-tags`): Give a variant that discriminated unions tag differently, such as one by a mapping key and one by the schema name, every tag they give it, so each union decodes the documents it selects the variant by. msgspec Structs take one tag, so they are unchanged.
- EncodedStr for constrained base64 strings (`--use-encoded-str-for-constrained-base64`): Write a format: byte string with a pattern or lengths in the field forms as an EncodedStr with the constraints in front of the decoding, so Pydantic 2.10 or later checks them on the base64 text.
- Length keywords read by type (`--read-length-keywords-by-type`): Read minLength, maxLength and pattern for strings only and minItems, maxItems and uniqueItems for arrays only, so a maxLength beside an array no longer limits how many items the list holds.
- msgspec union bounds read exactly (`--read-msgspec-union-bounds-exactly`): Decide whether the int member of a msgspec union with a number member drops its bounds on the bounds the schema writes, so a bound past 2**53 no longer rejects an integer the number member accepts.
- Model names taken from the schema (`--naming-strategy definitions-first`, `--name-allof-union-members-after-branches`, `--use-duplicate-name-suffix-for-every-collision`, `--capitalize-numbered-enum-members`, `--keep-first-character-of-path-keys`, `--name-converted-payloads-by-message`, `--singularize-last-word-of-item-names`): Give every definition its own name before an inline model that asks for it first, name the union members of an allOf after their branches, give the --duplicate-name-suffix suffix to every model renamed because its name is taken, capitalize the number of a capitalized enum member, strip only a leading slash from a paths key, name a converted AsyncAPI payload that names no type after its message, and singularize only the last word of an item model's name.
- Schema version read per document (`--read-schema-version-per-document`): Read each document by the schema version it declares, or the version of the document that references it, so the keywords beside a $ref and the version's features apply as that version says in every document of a run, and an OpenAPI 3.1 or later document reads them as JSON Schema 2020-12 does.
- Ignored $ref siblings left out (`--ignore-ref-siblings-by-schema-version`): Read a $ref as its target alone where the schema version ignores the keywords beside it (JSON Schema draft 4, 6 and 7, OpenAPI 3.0, AsyncAPI 2), so a sibling format: binary or uniqueItems no longer changes the type of a field.
- Combined schema keywords intersected (`--intersect-combined-schema-keywords`): Combine the keywords beside an anyOf or oneOf with each branch, merge an inherited override's nested properties name by name and by its narrowed type, read the $ref siblings, $ref aliases and null branches of allOf members and the required names an allOf adds to the one model it names, and keep no enum value that the merged type rejects, as JSON Schema validates them.
- allOf distributed over unions (`--distribute-allof-over-unions`): Give an allOf one union variant per combination of the branches of the anyOf and oneOf it holds, also through a $ref member and for their value branches, read a $ref branch with the allOf members and the value keywords beside it, and an OpenAPI body with an allOf beside an anyOf or oneOf as that union, as JSON Schema validates them.
- Reference null kept on merged models (`--keep-reference-null-on-merged-models`): Keep the null that the schema of a reference admits when its model is merged into an equal model that rejects null, so a `type: [object, null]` property keeps `| None` after duplicate removal or reuse.
- Meta for msgspec map keys (`--use-msgspec-meta-for-map-keys`): Write the keys of a msgspec map whose keys propertyNames or patternProperties constrain as Annotated[str, Meta(...)], so msgspec checks them.
- Submodules hidden by classes renamed (`--rename-submodules-hidden-by-classes`): Rename a submodule named like a class of its package, such as pkg/Warn.py beside the class Warn of pkg/__init__.py, to the first free name with trailing underscores, so importing it leaves the class in place.
- Unique items as sets by value (`--use-unique-items-as-set-by-value`): Under --use-unique-items-as-set, decide each set on the final item types and write one only where every value of its items hashes by value, and keep apart models whose arrays differ in uniqueItems.
- Constrained root models kept in every container (`--keep-constrained-root-models-in-every-container`): Under --collapse-root-models with --field-constraints, keep a constrained root model named inside any container of its holder, so a set, Sequence or Mapping keeps the constraints of its items.
- Enum literal aliases kept (`--keep-enum-literal-aliases`): Under --collapse-root-models, keep a named enum that the output writes as a Literal type alias named at its uses.
- Plain aliases of recursive models (`--use-plain-alias-for-recursive-models`): In Pydantic output, write a type alias whose whole value is a model that names itself as a plain TypeAlias, which every model that uses it builds.
- Whole types replaced by type overrides (`--type-overrides-replace-whole-type`): Make a class path of --type-overrides replace an object map itself (dict, not dict[str, dict]), and keep the item or property counts of the array or map an override replaces only where the new type counts the same.
- SerializeAsAny for every subclass (`--use-serialize-as-any-for-every-subclass`): Under --use-serialize-as-any, wrap a field in SerializeAsAny when any subclass of its model in the output adds fields, at any depth, after reuse merges the model and through its module.
- Dynamic anchors read in document order (`--read-dynamic-anchors-in-document-order`): Resolve a plain-name $dynamicRef that its dynamic scope does not bind, and a reference to a plain name several schemas declare, to the first declaration in document order, so the answer no longer depends on the order the schemas are parsed in.
- One model per reference site (`--use-one-model-per-ref-site`): Give an object $ref with sibling keywords one model per place it is written, which every unchanged copy of that place shares, so a chain of N definitions gives N-1 site models instead of N(N-1)/2, parsed without nesting.
- Escaped reference pointers read (`--read-escaped-ref-pointers`): Read the ~0 and ~1 escapes and the percent-encoded octets of a $ref JSON pointer as the characters they encode, so every spelling of a pointer names the one model of its target instead of a copy named after the escaped text.
- Pydantic dataclass fields read by alias (`--read-input-model-dataclass-fields-by-alias`): With --input-model, read the fields of a Pydantic dataclass by their aliases, as those of a model, so a field with an alias keeps its Python type, such as deque[int], like one without.
- Practical model structure and names (practical presets) (`--reuse-model`, `--collapse-reuse-models`, `--use-title-as-name`): Deduplicate identical models without empty inheritance wrappers and prefer schema titles for class names; the standard groups keep definitions ahead of inline duplicate names.

changes.summary:
They keep the options of the 20261104 presets and add:

- Dataclass arguments set to false written (`--keep-false-dataclass-arguments`): Write every dataclass decorator argument set to false, such as eq=False from --dataclass-arguments, instead of leaving it out, which gives it its default.
- Content parameters typed by their reference (`--keep-content-parameter-refs`): Type an OpenAPI parameter whose content media schema is a $ref by the model the $ref names, as a schema parameter is, instead of a copy of the referenced schema.
- Extension keys of paths skipped (`--skip-path-extension-keys`): In the paths scope, skip a key of paths that begins with x-, a specification extension and no path item, as the api scope does, so its operations get no models.
- Every reached input model type reused (`--reuse-every-reached-input-model-type`): With --input-model-ref-strategy reuse-all or reuse-foreign, reach the types to reuse through the fields of every model kind, dataclasses too, and import a type the Python type of a field already imports instead of writing an unused copy of it.
- x-python-type as written (`--use-x-python-type-as-written`): Write a field's x-python-type as given: a union spelled Optional[...] or Union[...] types the field as one spelled X | Y already does, instead of the schema's type, and a container class compatible with the schema, such as tuple or MutableSequence, is written around the schema's item types instead of list, Sequence, set, frozenset or Mapping.
- Typed nullable map values (`--use-typed-nullable-map-values`): Type the values of a map whose type array lists object alone or with null, such as [object, null], as its additionalProperties say instead of Any, and with --use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types of the 20261027 presets also those of a type array that lists object beside other types.
- Unknown fields forbidden by closed msgspec Structs (`--use-msgspec-forbid-unknown-fields`): Write forbid_unknown_fields=True on a msgspec Struct whose schema admits no property but its own (additionalProperties: false without patternProperties), so msgspec rejects the unknown fields the schema rejects.
- Reference null kept on collapsed root models (`--keep-reference-null-on-collapsed-root-models`): Under --collapse-root-models, keep the null of a root model that admits null where a field, item or map value that names it takes its type.
- allOf parents read in MRO order (`--read-allof-parents-in-mro-order`): Read the allOf parents of every inherited schema in the order of the class bases, so a property that several bases declare takes the nearer base's constraints and description, as the class does.
- Field options on every field (`--apply-field-options-to-every-field`): Give a GraphQL field, a property whose schema is true or false, a required name without a property and the tag field a discriminator appends the field options the other fields take, such as --use-default-kwarg, --use-annotated and --use-default-factory-for-optional-nested-models.
- Strict base64 strings (`--use-strict-str-for-base64`): Under --strict-types str, write a format: byte string as the StrictStr that EncodedStr decodes, so Pydantic 2.10 or later refuses bytes for it as for any other strict string, instead of Base64Str.
- Content media type strings as bytes (`--use-bytes-for-content-media-type`): Type a string of an OpenAPI document that has a contentMediaType and no contentEncoding, raw binary content, as bytes, as a format: binary string is, instead of str.
- Constrained string root models collapsed as Annotated (`--collapse-constrained-root-models-as-annotated`): Under --collapse-root-models with --use-annotated, inline a root model of a string with constraints into a union, list, dict or other container of its holder as Annotated[str, ...], which keeps the constraints on that member.
- Unused models removed beside type overrides (`--remove-unused-models-beside-type-overrides`): Remove the models nothing uses, such as an inlined root model, also from a module that a model-level --type-overrides key takes a model out of.
- Items of self-referencing arrays kept (`--keep-self-referencing-array-items`): Keep the items of an array whose items name the array itself (list[Node | Leaf] instead of list), except in msgspec output, which cannot decode such a type alias.
- Shared members kept on collapsed root models (`--keep-shared-members-on-collapsed-root-models`): Under --collapse-root-models, keep each member of a root type that collapse inlined at several sites at every site when a root model that member names is collapsed later, as a recursive union reaches its plain member.
- Operation enums written as Literal like definitions (`--use-enum-field-as-literal-in-operations`): Write the enum of an OpenAPI request body or response as a root model of a Literal where x-enum-field-as-literal, --enum-field-as-literal-map or --enum-field-as-literal writes a definition's enum so, instead of an Enum class.
- Request and response variants of numbered models deduplicated (`--dedupe-numbered-request-response-variants`): Under --read-only-write-only-model-type, merge a Request or Response variant of a numbered model, such as Page1Request of an inline copy Page1 of Page, into PageRequest where it renders the same, as the numbered model merges into Page.
- Defaults of inherited required fields kept (`--keep-defaults-of-inherited-required-fields`): With --use-default, keep the default a schema gives a property that only a schema it inherits from lists as required, as --use-default keeps that of a property the schema lists as required itself.
- Incomplete model defaults omitted (`--omit-incomplete-model-defaults`): Write a property whose object default lacks required fields of its model, such as default: {}, without that default, so input that leaves the property out is valid instead of failing on the default.
- AsyncAPI message trait headers merged (`--merge-message-trait-headers`): Give an AsyncAPI message the headers of all its traits, merged in order as JSON Merge Patches, inline and referenced traits alike, and then its own headers, which win.

changes.summary:
They keep the options of the 20261111 presets and add:

- Object keywords by type (`--read-object-keywords-by-type`): Read the keywords that constrain objects only beside an anyOf or oneOf for the branches that admit objects, so a string, const or enum branch beside patternProperties stays itself.
changes.title: New dated presets `standard-py3XX-20261112` and `practical-py3XX-20261112`

changes.migrate: Parse the raw body, or use the stream helper regenerated clients get at `client.protocols.<resource>.<method>`, which yields typed items.
changes.summary: For an OpenAPI 3.2 response whose `text/event-stream`, JSON Lines or NDJSON media has only an `itemSchema`, the operation method, its `with_response` view and its result type alias read the whole body raw: `str` for an event stream and `bytes` for JSON Lines or NDJSON, where they returned the model of the item schema's array projection.
changes.title: Generated client methods return the raw body of `itemSchema` stream responses

changes.migrate: Rename the declared helper.
changes.summary: Generation derives a stream helper named `<resource>.<method>` for each OpenAPI 3.2 operation that streams an `itemSchema`. A helper of the protocols helper file whose name contains a derived name, or is contained in one, now fails generation with an `E_NAME_COLLISION` config diagnostic.
changes.title: A protocols helper whose name collides with a derived stream helper is refused

changes.migrate: Annotate, `isinstance`-check or match stream items against the referenced model instead of `models.ItemSchema` or `models.ItemSchemaModel`.
changes.summary: SSE, JSON Lines and NDJSON stream helpers whose `itemSchema` is a bare `$ref` use the referenced model, for example `EventStream[models.LogEntry]`, instead of the `ItemSchema` or `ItemSchemaModel` model generated at the item schema location. With Pydantic v2 output, decoded items are instances of the referenced model.
changes.title: Generated client stream helpers type items as the model their `itemSchema` references

changes.migrate: Filter the notices by category and message, or by your calling module, for example `warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning, module="mypackage.models")`.
changes.summary: Notices of the deprecation registry are attributed to the outermost frame outside the package (your module that called `generate()`, or the console script) instead of a module inside it. Filters that match them by `module="datamodel_code_generator"` no longer suppress them, and a script that calls the API directly may now show `DeprecationWarning` notices that were hidden.
changes.title: Deprecation and migration notices name the code that called datamodel-code-generator

keep.note: No option writes the old output without the property: `--graphql-no-typename` also removes the `typename__` field, which the 0.95.0 output had, so serialization and validation change with it.

changes.summary: Each model generated from a GraphQL object type has a `__typename` property that returns its `typename__` field, so graphql-core's default type resolver resolves unions and interfaces from model instances without a `resolve_type` function. The property is written for `pydantic_v2.BaseModel`, `pydantic_v2.dataclass`, `dataclasses.dataclass` and `msgspec.Struct` output; input and interface types, `typing.TypedDict` output and custom model templates do not get it. Fields, aliases and validation are unchanged.
changes.title: GraphQL object models gain a read-only `__typename` property

keep.note: No option restores the 0.95.0 reading; `--model-name-map` can pin individual names.

changes.summary: An `anyOf` or `oneOf` branch that is a `const`, an `enum`, a nested `allOf`, `anyOf` or `oneOf`, a false schema or a `$ref` to such a schema no longer takes the sibling object keywords, so such a site becomes a union, which adds enum classes and can renumber model names (`Owner` becomes `Owner1`). The standard and practical 20261112 presets turn the option on.
changes.title: `--read-object-keywords-by-type` also reads `const`, `enum` and `allOf` branches as admitting no object

changes.summary: `constr(pattern=r'^it\'s$')` is written `constr(pattern=r"^it's$")`: Python's `re` matches the same values, and `model_json_schema()` publishes the schema's pattern unchanged. Snapshot tests and committed generated code show the new text after regenerating.
changes.title: Patterns holding a quote are written without an escaped quote

changes.migrate: Write the format as the AsyncAPI specification lists it (`application/schema+json;version=draft-07`) and the content type as a media type (`application/x+json`).
changes.summary: A channel is now left out with a `message_content_types` warning where an AsyncAPI 2 message trait gives a `schemaFormat` that generation does not read, such as `application/schema;version=draft-07`, which generation refuses when the message itself gives it, or where a message's `contentType` is no media type but ends in `+json` (`x+json`). Such channels were generated with a JSON codec.
changes.title: Generated AsyncAPI clients leave out a channel whose payload format generation does not read

changes.migrate: Catch `datamodel_code_generator.Error` where the code caught `PresetError` around a target run.
changes.summary: With `generate_server` or `generate_client`, a `preset` that does not match `target_python_version` raises `datamodel_code_generator.Error`, as a model-only run does, with the same message. It raised `datamodel_code_generator.preset.PresetError`, which is not an `Error`. The command line is unchanged.
changes.title: `generate()` with a server or client target raises `Error` for a preset that does not fit

changes.summary: The query and header parameters of a channel's handshake are now the fields of the models generated for its binding's `query` and `headers` objects, required where the models require them, and the subprotocols a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header offers, or the `Accept` header that makes a channel a server-sent event stream, are the values the header's type admits. A channel is now generated whose `query` or `headers` object is written with `allOf`, or with keywords beside its properties such as `$schema`, `examples`, `default`, `minProperties` or `deprecated`, or that names a required property it does not declare; such channels were skipped as `websocket_bindings` or `server_sent_events`. Channels at one address whose handshakes write a parameter alike but whose models type it differently, such as a `$ref` that names a schema of another document through an `allOf`, are still left out as `shared_addresses`. A `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header written as a `oneOf` of `const`s, also one a referenced schema holds whose models are a root model or alias of a union of `Literal`s (a `oneOf` of `$ref`s to `const` schemas), now offers each value, where it offered none (and a required one left the channel out), and an `Accept` header written so now opens the channel as a server-sent event stream. An AsyncAPI 2 operation whose HTTP binding comes from a trait under `components/operationTraits` now gives its parameters, where its channel was skipped; an operation's own binding, which no model types, still leaves the channel out, with the message `the query schema of its HTTP binding has no model`. A parameter written as a `$ref` now takes the `description` of the schema it names. Under `--force-optional` the models require no parameter, so every handshake parameter is now optional; a required header that the client writes itself, on a WebSocket handshake or on the GET that opens a server-sent event stream (such as `Host`, `Upgrade`, or a free-form `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, which then offers no subprotocol), no longer leaves the channel out, and two bindings that declare one parameter required and optional now agree, where the channel was skipped.
changes.title: Generated AsyncAPI clients read handshake parameters and fixed header values from the models

changes.summary: With `--ignore-ref-siblings-by-schema-version`, an AsyncAPI 2 handshake query or header parameter whose property writes a `default` beside its `$ref` no longer takes that default as its argument default, as the generated models do not; it takes the default the referenced schema gives, or none (`token: str = 'abc'` becomes `token: str | UNSET = UNSET`). Without the option the client keeps the sibling default, as the models do.
changes.title: Generated AsyncAPI 2 clients follow the models for a default beside a handshake parameter's `$ref`

changes.summary: How a message travels now follows the models generated for its payload, as an OpenAPI body of its media type does. A text message (`text/plain`, `text/csv`, `text/xml`, `text/html`, ...) whose models type a string, such as an enum of strings, `type: [string]`, a nullable string, a `const` or an `allOf` of a string schema, or a string with `contentEncoding`, is now sent and received as `str`; such channels were skipped as `message_content_types`. A message of another binary media type (`image/png`, `application/xml`, `application/x-msgpack`, ...), which a frame carries as its raw bytes, is now sent and received as `bytes` whatever its schema (as `str` where its models type an enum of strings), where it was skipped unless it was a binary string. A message of a form media type (`multipart/form-data`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) is still sent and received as `bytes` only where its models type its payload as raw bytes (a binary string), and its channel is still skipped otherwise. A JSON message on a WebSocket channel whose payload is a binary string (`type: string, format: binary`) is now raw `bytes` in a binary frame instead of the payload's model; on a server-sent event channel its data is still decoded by the model. An `application/octet-stream` message whose payload is an enum of strings, and a text message whose binary string the models type as `str` (`--type-mappings binary=string`), are now `str` instead of `bytes`.
changes.title: Generated AsyncAPI clients code a message as the models type its payload

changes.summary: A channel is now generated whose message payload names its `schemaFormat` in another case or with spaces (`application/SCHEMA+JSON;version=draft-07`, `application/schema+json ; version=draft-07`), in an OpenAPI format (`application/vnd.oai.openapi;version=3.0.0`), or in such a spelling through an AsyncAPI 2 message trait; such channels were skipped as `message_content_types`. A payload written `{schema: ...}` without a `schemaFormat` now binds the model generated for its `schema`: where it was the channel's only message, generation failed (`The use has no generated native type`), and beside another JSON message the channel was skipped as `several_messages` (`a message's payload declares no type`). Avro, Protocol Buffers and XML Schema payloads, also when a trait gives the format, stay left out.
changes.title: Generated AsyncAPI clients read a payload's schema format and wrapper as the models do

changes.summary: A `pattern` whose character class ends a range with a class escape or a Unicode property (`^[a-\w]+$`, `[a-\pL]`, `[a-\p{L}]`) was written as the schema writes it, and the module failed at import with `invalid range boundary, must be a literal` (a `msgspec.Struct` failed when it first decoded the type with `bad character range`): Pydantic's default regex engine refuses a range that ends with a class, and Python's `re` rejects it too. The pattern is now left out with a warning, as `^[\w- ]*$` (a class as the start of a range) has been since 0.92.0, and the model checks the other keywords only. A hyphen that makes no range keeps its pattern (`^[a-z0-9-\s]+$`, `^[^-\w]+$`). Output that imported and decoded before is unchanged.

changes.summary: A `pattern` that every pydantic-core release from 2.0 to 2.50 refuses for size, but that the size check counted below the limit, was written as the schema writes it, and the module failed at import with `Compiled regex exceeds size limit`: a class of several Unicode general categories (`[\p{L}\p{N}_-]{1,256}`, `^[\p{L}\p{Z}\p{N}_.:/=+\-@]{0,256}$`), `\p{Lu}` or `\p{Ll}`, a count that passes the limit only with what the ASCII characters of its atom and its optional copies add (`^\p{L}{1,256}$`, `^.{0,10240}$`, `^[^<>]{1,10000}$`), a counted group of single atoms (`^(?:[\w-]\.?){1,128}@(?:[\w-]\.?){1,128}$`) and an alternation without `^` or `$` in which every branch holds at least one copy of these classes or escapes outside a group (`user-[\w-]{1,128}|group-[\w-]{1,128}`). The model now selects `regex_engine="python-re"` for it; a pattern Python's `re` rejects too, as it rejects `\p{...}`, is left out with a warning. Only patterns that every pydantic-core release from 2.0 to 2.50 refuses are read this way. Output that imported before is unchanged.
changes.title: More patterns past the regex size limit no longer fail at import, such as `^\p{L}{1,256}$`, `^.{0,10240}$` and `[\p{L}\p{N}_-]{1,256}`

The model now selects `regex_engine="python-re"` for it; a pattern Python's `re` rejects too, as it rejects `\p{...}`, is left out with a warning. That is what a single repetition past the limit has got since 0.92.0. Only patterns that every pydantic-core release from 2.0 to 2.50 refuses are read this way. changes.summary: Two changes, both under `--parent-scoped-naming`. (1) With `--naming-strategy numbered`, `primary-first` or `definitions-first`, a method, handler or class name that another name in its scope already holds now takes the name of its enclosing scope in front of it instead of a number (`get_a_b_1` becomes `default_get_a_b`, `GetAB1` becomes `DefaultGetAB`). (2) With `--naming-strategy full-path`, such a name now takes both prefixes, as the models' class names do (row `legacy-both-prefixes`, #5666): `item_store_get_item` becomes `item_store_item_store_get_item`, `ItemStoreGetItemResponse` becomes `ItemStoreItemStoreGetItemResponse`.
changes.title: Generated clients and servers name colliding API names as the models' naming strategies do

changes.migrate: Set `use-annotated = false` in `pyproject.toml` instead of passing `--no-use-annotated`, or pass `--read-implied-options-from-merged-values` (the 20261113 presets turn it on), under which the argument turns `--field-constraints` off as the key does.
changes.summary: The command line reads the values of `pyproject.toml` before it applies the arguments, so with `use-annotated = true` and `field-constraints = false` there, `--no-use-annotated` turns `--use-annotated` off and leaves `--field-constraints` on, which `use-annotated = true` turned on. Such a run now reports it with a `UserWarning` that names the key and `--read-implied-options-from-merged-values`; the option stays on as before and the generated output is unchanged. A caller that turns warnings into errors gets an error.
changes.title: An argument that turns off an option `pyproject.toml` turned on, whose implied option stays on, emits a `UserWarning`

changes.summary: Draft 7 and older have no `$defs` keyword, so their meta-schemas do not constrain its members. In a document read in one of these versions (the version of the input document, or of each document under `--read-schema-version-per-document`), a member of `$defs` whose value is neither an object nor a boolean, such as a `description` string written beside the definitions, is now skipped with a `UserWarning` that names it, and the document is generated; it was refused before. Such a member is still refused in a document read as 2019-09 or later (a document without `$schema` that holds `$defs` reads as 2020-12) and where a reference names it. A caller that turns warnings into errors gets an error.
changes.title: A member of `$defs` that is not a schema is skipped with a `UserWarning` in a draft 7 or older document

changes.migrate: Pass `--read-ids-with-empty-fragment` (the 20261113 presets turn it on), or write the `$id` without the `#`.
changes.summary: Where a document declares an `$id` with an empty fragment (`https://example.com/item.json#`) and a `$ref` in it names that URI, the generator loads the document at that URL, as before, and now first warns with a `SchemaResourceRefWarning` that names the URL, the `$id` and `--read-ids-with-empty-fragment`, under which the reference resolves inside the document; the generated output is unchanged. A caller that turns warnings into errors gets an error.
changes.title: A `$ref` to its document's `$id` written with an empty fragment emits a `SchemaResourceRefWarning` before the fetch

changes.migrate: Turn the other option off as the warning says, for example with `--no-intersect-combined-schema-keywords`, or drop the value that turns the option off.
changes.summary: `--use-annotated` turns `--field-constraints` on, `--use-type-alias-type` turns `--use-type-alias` on and `--intersect-combined-schema-keywords` turns `--intersect-allof-keywords` on, also where a preset sets the first option. A run that turns the second option off (`--no-intersect-allof-keywords`, `false` in `pyproject.toml`, `False` given to `generate()`) is now reported with a `UserWarning` that names both options and how to turn both off; the option stays on as before and the generated output is unchanged. A `false` in `pyproject.toml` is not reported under a `--preset` argument whose preset sets that option, as such a preset replaces the values of `pyproject.toml`. `generate()` does not report `use_type_alias`, nor a value of a config that `load_pyproject_config()` returned. A caller that turns warnings into errors gets an error.
changes.title: An option that is turned off and that another option turns on emits a `UserWarning`

changes.summary: A document whose root has a `swagger` key and no `openapi` key is read as YAML or JSON data when `--input-file-type` is not given, and the OpenAPI reader finds no model in it, as it reads `components/schemas`, not the `definitions` of Swagger 2.0. The notice that names the inferred type now adds a line that the input looks like a Swagger 2.0 document, which is read as data, and that its definitions are read as JSON Schema with `--input-file-type jsonschema`. The refusal `Models not found in the input data` of such a document under `--input-file-type openapi` continues with the cause and what to do. The inferred type, the generated output and every document that generates are unchanged.
changes.title: A Swagger 2.0 document is named in the notice of the inferred input type and in the refusal of `--input-file-type openapi`

changes.title: `--type-overrides` keys that match no model or field emit a `UserWarning`

changes.summary: With `--field-include-all-keys`, a `$ref` to an array schema with `contains` beside it wrote `contains`, `minContains` and `maxContains` into `json_schema_extra` in an order that depended on the hash seed of the process, so one command gave either of two files and `--check` failed at random. They are now written in the order the schema writes them. The models behave the same: only the order of the keys of the `json_schema_extra` dict changes, to one of the two orders earlier runs produced.
changes.title: `--field-include-all-keys` writes the contains keywords beside a `$ref` in the order of the schema

changes.summary: Write a oneOf or anyOf that declares no discriminator as a discriminated union (Pydantic Field(discriminator=...), msgspec tagged structs) when every branch that is not null requires one property holding one string or integer value (a const or a one-value enum, also through allOf members and local $refs), with no value shared; in Pydantic output a union with a discriminator keyword keeps it. Valid payloads parse the same, except that a tag typed as a one-value enum class becomes its Literal value; with --use-one-literal-as-default a payload without the tag, which the schema requires, is rejected. An invalid payload reports the errors of the branch its tag names, or one tag error. Not applied to dataclasses.dataclass and typing.TypedDict output. Without it these unions are smart unions in Pydantic output, and msgspec output tags only the unions whose tags are written on the branches themselves, as in 0.96.0
changes.title: New option `--infer-union-discriminators` (`--no-infer-union-discriminators`)

changes.summary: Base classes that open the Enum classes of open enums (--open-enums), by the class the enum is written on (JSON or JSON file path). Keys: Enum, StrEnum, IntEnum. Example: '{"StrEnum": "mypkg.OpenStrEnum", "IntEnum": "mypkg.OpenIntEnum"}'. Each is your member-less subclass of that class whose _missing_ keeps a value it does not list; a value type before Enum (--use-subclass-enum) stays: (str, mypkg.OpenEnum). An open enum whose class has no entry, or that is written as a Literal, is written as Literal[...] joined with its type
changes.title: New option `--open-enum-base-class-map`

changes.summary: Accept values an enum does not list. extensible: the enums whose schema marks them open (x-extensible-enum: true, or x-ms-enum with modelAsString: true); all: every enum of two or more values, except one whose schema closes it (x-extensible-enum: false, modelAsString: false); none: no enum, as without the option. An open enum is written as its Enum class on the base --open-enum-base-class-map names for that class, else as Literal[...] joined with its type (Literal['red', 'green'] | str), whatever the options say about Literals
changes.title: New option `--open-enums`

changes.summary: Read the format of a schema as an annotation, as JSON Schema does: a string, integer or number schema takes the type its type keyword gives (str, int, float), with its own length, pattern and bound keywords, so every value the schema accepts validates, a string or integer dumps as written (a number as the float it parses to, as without a format), and an unknown format gives no warning; a format that a --type-mappings entry names for the schema's type keeps that mapping, and format: binary stays bytes. Without it each known format selects a type (EmailStr, AwareDatetime, UUID, Decimal, SecretStr, Base64Str, ...), as in 0.96.0
changes.title: New option `--read-format-as-annotation` (`--no-read-format-as-annotation`)

changes.summary: Read an $id that ends with an empty fragment, such as https://example.com/item.json#, as the URI without it, which names the same resource, so a $ref to https://example.com/item.json# or https://example.com/item.json#/definitions/Tag in the document that declares it resolves inside that document; without it such a $ref loads the document at that URL, from the network, as in 0.96.0.
changes.title: New option `--read-ids-with-empty-fragment` (`--no-read-ids-with-empty-fragment`)

changes.summary: Read the options that another option turns on (--use-annotated turns on --field-constraints) from the arguments and pyproject.toml together, so --no-use-annotated over use-annotated = true in pyproject.toml also leaves --field-constraints off where pyproject.toml gives it false, as use-annotated = false there does; without it --field-constraints stays on, as in 0.96.0.
changes.title: New option `--read-implied-options-from-merged-values` (`--no-read-implied-options-from-merged-values`)

changes.summary: With --intersect-combined-schema-keywords, give a property that a model only makes required the schema its allOf parents declare, read in the order of the class bases from the allOf members the model's own fields are read from (an alias member followed to the schema it names, the keywords beside a $ref member read with it), so a model written before its parents takes the field it takes when written after them; without it the declaration is looked up in the allOf members as written, and under --intersect-combined-schema-keywords such a field can lose its description or its constraints or become Any, as in 0.96.0
changes.title: New option `--read-inherited-property-schemas-in-mro-order` (`--no-read-inherited-property-schemas-in-mro-order`)

changes.summary: Read the Kubernetes schema extensions as the keywords they stand for: x-kubernetes-int-or-string (and the int-or-string format) as an integer or a string, x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields beside properties as additionalProperties true, and an x-kubernetes-group-version-kind as the const and default of the apiVersion and kind it names; without it they are ignored, as in 0.96.0
changes.title: New option `--read-kubernetes-extensions` (`--no-read-kubernetes-extensions`)

changes.summary: Read the target of the one $ref of an allOf as every other $ref is read: in the document that holds the schema, a plain-name anchor such as #code included. The target decides whether the schema is typed as the referenced enum, as a root model over it, or refused, so a schema of a referenced file takes the form the same schemas take in one file; without it the target is read at the same pointer of the input document, where a plain-name anchor names nothing, so such a schema can be written as a copy of the enum or refused, as in 0.96.0.
changes.title: New option `--read-single-allof-refs-in-their-documents` (`--no-read-single-allof-refs-in-their-documents`)

changes.summary: Read an unquoted YAML value with _ or : that YAML 1.1 reads as a number, such as 16:9 (969 in base 60), 18_24 or 1_000, as its text, as YAML 1.2, which OpenAPI names, and the ryaml reader read it, also in enum, default, const, examples, extensions and YAML data input. Without it such a value is the number YAML 1.1 reads, as in 0.96.0, except where a string is required in a document that the number makes invalid (a pattern, a format, a description, a component or property name), where it is its text.
changes.title: New option `--read-yaml-1-1-numbers-as-text` (`--no-read-yaml-1-1-numbers-as-text`)

changes.summary: Write each value the schema leaves untyped ({}, true, a schema whose keywords give it no type, the values of an object without properties and the items of an array without items) as this type instead of Any: pydantic.JsonValue (Pydantic 2.5 or later), object, Any or the dotted import path of a type of your own, which the models import; the structure is as without the option. --type-overrides, x-python-type and x-python-import keep their types, and msgspec.Struct output keeps Any, which msgspec decodes into JSON values. Without it untyped values are Any, and object in containers under --use-object-type, as in 0.96.0
changes.title: New option `--untyped-value-type`

changes.summary: Type every reference to a schema with x-python-import by the class it imports, as a $ref to it at a field is: also an allOf of it beside keywords that add no field where a JSON pointer into another document or a whole-document $ref names it, and under --read-only-write-only-model-type request-response a model does not split for the readOnly or writeOnly properties of such a schema, nor for those its allOf bases reach through one; without it such a reference keeps the model of its schema and those models split, as in 0.96.0
changes.title: New option `--use-x-python-import-for-every-ref` (`--no-use-x-python-import-for-every-ref`)

changes.summary:
They keep the options of the 20261112 presets and add:

- x-python-import for every reference (`--use-x-python-import-for-every-ref`): Type every reference to a schema with x-python-import by the class it imports, also an allOf of one in another document, and split no request/response model for the readOnly or writeOnly properties of such a schema.
- Extensible enums accept new values (`--open-enums extensible`): Accept the values an API adds to an enum its schema marks extensible (x-extensible-enum: true, x-ms-enum modelAsString: true), written as Literal[...] joined with its type, such as Literal['red', 'green'] | str, instead of rejecting them.
- Discriminators inferred from tags (`--infer-union-discriminators`): Write a oneOf or anyOf without a discriminator as a discriminated union where every branch that is not null requires one property with one string or integer value, also in its allOf members; valid payloads parse the same, an invalid one reports the errors of the branch its tag names.
- Kubernetes extensions read (`--read-kubernetes-extensions`): Read x-kubernetes-int-or-string as an integer or a string, x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields beside properties as extra keys kept, and an x-kubernetes-group-version-kind as the one apiVersion and kind a resource takes, so the models accept and keep what Kubernetes does.
- Inherited property schemas read in MRO order (`--read-inherited-property-schemas-in-mro-order`): Give a property that a model only makes required the schema its allOf parents declare, read in the order of the class bases from the allOf members the model's fields are read from, so a model written before its parents takes the field it takes when written after them.
- Ids with an empty fragment read as their documents (`--read-ids-with-empty-fragment`): Read an absolute-URL $id written with an empty fragment, such as https://example.com/item.json#, as the URI without it, so a $ref to it resolves inside the document that declares it instead of loading the document at that URL from the network. A relative $id is not matched: a $ref to it reads the file.
- YAML 1.1-only numbers read as text (`--read-yaml-1-1-numbers-as-text`): Read an unquoted YAML value with _ or : that YAML 1.1 reads as a number, such as 16:9 or 18_24, as its text, as YAML 1.2, which OpenAPI names, and the ryaml reader do, so an enum of aspect ratios keeps the values '16:9' and '4:3' instead of the integers 969 and 243.
- Implied options read from the merged values (`--read-implied-options-from-merged-values`): Read the options that another option turns on from the arguments and pyproject.toml together, so --no-use-annotated over use-annotated = true in pyproject.toml also leaves --field-constraints off where pyproject.toml gives it false, as use-annotated = false there does.
- Single allOf references read in their documents (`--read-single-allof-refs-in-their-documents`): Read the target of an allOf of one $ref in the document that holds the schema, a plain-name anchor such as #code included, as every other $ref is read, so a schema of a referenced file is typed as a root model over the referenced enum, as the same schemas in one file are, instead of a copy of the enum; a valid referenced file is no longer refused where the input document holds false at that pointer, and a true target there is a root model that accepts every value.
- Untyped values as JSON values (practical presets) (`--untyped-value-type pydantic.JsonValue`): Write each value the schema leaves untyped as pydantic.JsonValue instead of Any, the typed form of the object the practical groups prefer for unconstrained values: a JSON document parses to the same values, and Python values that are no JSON values, such as a datetime or a set, are rejected.
changes.title: New dated presets `standard-py3XX-20261113` and `practical-py3XX-20261113`

changes.summary: With `--generate-client`, explicit argument names (`parameter_names`, `--aliases`), method names (`name` of `--client-operations`, sorted within each resource) or the `resource` of channel settings that take one name three or more times report it once instead of once per repeat, and several such names are reported in sorted order after the reserved-name and `--aliases` diagnostics of the operation's parameters (`The arguments of GET /items take 'b' twice; ... take 'a' twice` becomes `... take 'a' twice; ... take 'b' twice`); the "names no parameter" error still follows them. An explicit method name that is a reserved member name (`close`) taken twice is reported as reserved only, without the collision line. Servers already reported collisions this way.
changes.title: Generated clients report a name that explicit names take twice once, sorted, as servers do

changes.summary: With `--collapse-root-models` and `--output-model-type msgspec.Struct`, a root model whose references are all collapsed into their users (several fields, some naming it inside a union) was still written as an unused module-level type alias (`NullableShort: TypeAlias = Annotated[str, Meta(max_length=3)] | None`); it is no longer written. Nothing named the alias, so the models that used it are unchanged and validate the same payloads.
changes.title: Root models every use of which is collapsed are no longer written as unused aliases under msgspec

changes.summary: With `--generate-schema-validators` (or `--schema-validator-type pydantic-v2`), a const or enum that holds a number equal to a boolean (`0`, `1`) or a boolean gets a check on the raw input: `true` for `const: 1`, for `enum: [1, 2]` or for `enum: [1, "x"]`, and `1` for `const: true`, which Python's `True == 1` let the Literal or Enum take, are now rejected, as JSON Schema rejects them; `1.0` for `const: 1` is still accepted, and an enum that holds both (`[1, true]`) takes both. The check holds for properties, array items and mapping values, for an Enum class a property references, for the consts of a oneOf or anyOf (with branches that take no boolean or number, such as `null`), and for root models; models gain `__json_schema_constant_types__` and a shared base with `_validate_json_schema_constant_types`. Without the option nothing changes.
changes.title: Schema validators reject a boolean for a numeric const or enum value and a number for a boolean one

changes.summary: With `--generate-server`, a form body the server reads through its own adapter (multipart, or URL-encoded with `pydantic_v2.dataclass`) also reads each member by its field name only where the configuration the model applies sets `populate_by_name` or `validate_by_name`, with the bases as Pydantic applies them (a model merges its bases' in order, then its own; a dataclass takes its own, else its first base's). A model whose base sets it while the model turns it off (`--extra-template-data` with `populate_by_name: false`), or a dataclass with a configuration of its own under such a base, no longer lists the field names (`FieldPlan('last_name', ...)` beside `FieldPlan('last-name', ...)`); the model dropped the values read under those names, so requests are handled as before. A class written with `--class-decorators` now counts too: a multipart body `Person` with the property `first-name` under `--allow-population-by-field-name --class-decorators @typing.final --additional-imports typing` lists `FieldPlan('first_name', 'string')`, and a part named `first_name` still reaches `Person(first_name='b')`.
changes.title: Generated servers read a form member by its field name exactly where the model's applied configuration validates by name, a decorated model included

changes.summary: With `--generate-server`, an exploded `form` query parameter or a cookie parameter typed by a Pydantic model or dataclass, and an exploded styled member of a form body, took every key no other parameter or member declares, by its schema's `additionalProperties`. Where the configuration the model applies says `extra='forbid'` or `'ignore'` (a class that sets no `extra` ignores them), it now takes none; declared parameters (`reserved_names`) are never taken, as before. For `GET /plain?count=1&foo=bar` with `count` declared and `obj` typed by `Plain` (properties `size`, no `additionalProperties`), the handler now gets `obj=None` where it got `Plain(size=None)`, and a cookie object `prefs` of the same type is `None` for a request that carries only other cookies (`_ga=x`), where it was `Plain(size=None)`; with `--extra-fields forbid` such requests are served (`obj=None`, `prefs=None`) where the model refused them with 422 although the object was not sent; with `--extra-fields ignore` an object whose schema says `additionalProperties: true` no longer takes `foo` either. A required object that receives only undeclared keys (`GET /required?foo=bar`) is now missing (422) where it was `Plain(size=None)`, as `--extra-fields forbid` already answered. Two such parameters without `additionalProperties` in one operation, or one beside a `deepObject` parameter, which stopped the server with "Expanded query parameter names collide", now generate and serve `?size=1&page=2`. With `--extra-fields allow` nothing changes: an object takes the keys and cookies its schema allows (with no `additionalProperties`, every unclaimed one), and two such parameters still stop the server.
changes.title: Generated servers no longer attribute unclaimed query keys and cookies to an exploded query or cookie object whose model drops other members

changes.summary: With `--output-model-type pydantic_v2.dataclass`, a dataclass keeps extra members only where the configuration Pydantic applies to it says `extra='allow'`: its own configuration, or, where it has none, its first base's. The client codec (`extras_serializer`), the server response (`dump=extras_json`, with the `primary` status it adds) and the copies of `_runtime/model_codecs/pydantic_extras.py` (a server's `shared.py` too) now follow that. A class written with `--class-decorators` now counts as well: for `Thing` with `additionalProperties: true` used as a JSON body and response, under `--class-decorators @typing.final --additional-imports typing` the client sends `{"v":"a","foo":"b"}` for `Thing(v='a', foo='b')` where it sent `{"v":"a"}`, and the server returns the extra members too. A dataclass with a configuration of its own that sets no `extra` (for example `validate_by_name` from `--allow-population-by-field-name`) under a base with `additionalProperties: true`, and a dataclass whose first base forbids extra members, no longer take `extras_serializer` or `dump=extras_json`; Pydantic kept no extra members in them, so their JSON does not change.
changes.title: Generated clients and servers write the extra members of a Pydantic dataclass exactly where the configuration it applies keeps them, a decorated one included

changes.summary: Whether a form body, a client's form or query object parameter, or a multipart body typed by a Pydantic model or dataclass takes members besides its properties now also follows the configuration the model applies, with its bases as Pydantic applies them: where it says `extra='forbid'` or `'ignore'` (a class that sets no `extra` ignores them) the body takes none; otherwise, `--extra-fields allow` included, it takes what the first `additionalProperties` among its schema and its bases' gives, as before, and nothing changes under `--extra-fields allow`. An object without `additionalProperties`, or any object under `--extra-fields forbid` or `ignore`, no longer has `additional=FieldPlan('', 'string')` in a client's form or query plan, `additional=PartPlan('', 'json')` (and its `parts=`) in a client's multipart body sent whole, nor `additional=JsonPart('', TypeAdapter(object), untyped=True)` in a server's; the model held no other members to write, and unknown parts still reach it on a server (`forbid` answers 422, `ignore` drops them), so the requests sent and the values handled do not change, and a client call option no longer counts the undeclared names of such an object as written by its pagination. With `--extra-fields ignore` or `forbid`, a server no longer checks other members against the type their `additionalProperties` gives them: under `ignore` the model drops them and the request is served, under `forbid` it is still answered with 422 (`extra_forbidden` or `unexpected_keyword_argument`). With both backends, a multipart body whose other members are typed as an object gets `x=abc` served under `ignore` (before 422 `json_invalid`, and `model_type` or `dict_type` for `x=5`); with `pydantic_v2.dataclass`, a URL-encoded or multipart body typed `{type: integer}` gets `x=abc` served too (before 422 `int_parsing`). Three refusals go. A URL-encoded body whose `additionalProperties` is an object, refused under `ignore` and `forbid` ("A parameter value needs one unambiguous scalar kind"), now generates. Under the default options, `ignore` and `forbid`, a URL-encoded or multipart body with an exploded object member without `additionalProperties` beside another such member or beside a member that allows other properties (such as a map), and one beside a `deepObject` member, which were refused ("The exploded form member ... allows other properties ..."), now generate: `size=1&k=v&j=w` reaches the handler as `page=Page(size=1)`, `filter={'k': 'v', 'j': 'w'}`. Under `--extra-fields ignore` and `forbid` this also holds for exploded members typed by a model whose schema says `additionalProperties: true` or gives a schema. A multipart body the client sends as parts (`MultipartBody`) and a multipart response it reads into `MultipartData` keep the other parts the schema allows, as before. With `pydantic_v2.dataclass`, a dataclass with a configuration of its own that sets no `extra` no longer takes the typed other members of a base's schema.
changes.title: Generated clients and servers no longer take other members of a form or multipart body, or a client query object, that the model drops

changes.summary: With `--collapse-root-models` under msgspec.Struct, the warning that a root-model alias whose references are all collapsed is generated without some member constraints (`... Parted is generated without these constraints.`) is no longer printed, since that unused alias is no longer written (see collapsed-root-unused-alias); the warnings of the fields that use it stay.
changes.title: No dropped-constraints warning for a collapsed root model that is no longer written

changes.summary: Generation of request and response models with an intersect option no longer fails with "A Parser can not resolve classes" for a $ref to a closed object beside a schema-valued additionalProperties.
changes.title: Request/response models no longer crash on a $ref to a closed object beside a schema-valued additionalProperties
